question: What is the discount on a product with a list price of ₹3,000 and a discount rate of 25%?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A discount of 25% is equivalent to the fraction 1/4.

Discount = (1/4) × List Price

⇒ Discount = (1/4) × 3000

⇒ Discount = 750

**∴ The correct answer is ₹750.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

List Price = ₹3,000

Discount Rate = 25%

**Formula Used:**

Discount = (Discount % ÷ 100) × List Price

 
 List Price
 ₹3000
 
 
 Selling Price
 ₹2250
 
 
• 
 

 
 − 25% Discount
 Discount: ₹750

**Calculations:**

⇒ Discount = (25 ÷ 100) × 3000

⇒ Discount = 0.25 × 3000

⇒ Discount = 750

**∴ The correct answer is ₹750.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Selling Price Formula

Selling Price = List Price − Discount.

Successive Discounts

When two consecutive discounts D₁% and D₂% are given, the equivalent single discount is [D₁ + D₂ − (D₁ × D₂) ÷ 100]%.

Markup Percentage

Marked Price is generally set above the Cost Price to allow for discounts while still making a profit. Markup % = [(MP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100.
